look_here_first: A small WIRY grama with thin branching stems and typically TWO TO SEVEN narrow branches that lie quite close to the axis (APPRESSED). Many flowering parts are red to purplish, but do not rely on color. On a magnified spikelet inspect the three awns that give 'threeawn grama' its name; the awn count is not proven from the distant photos.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hagenbuch & Lemke's Texas Hill Country grass treatment documents specimen records from Blanco, Comal, Edwards, Hays, Gillespie, Kimble, Llano, Uvalde, and Val Verde counties.

best_field_traits: very narrow mostly basal leaf blades
2–7 persistent red or purplish pectinate branches
branches slender and appressed to main axis
spikelets bear three short rough awns
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with B. hirsuta and B. pectinata, B. trifida is much smaller and more wiry, with slender appressed reddish branches rather than broad eyebrow-like combs.
crew_field_steps: Use the finger-scale field macro to find the thin greenish flowering axis and the long skinny appressed reddish branchlets, not broad eyebrow combs.
Find an entire flowering stem and inspect how its few narrow lateral branches hug rather than spread widely from the main axis.
Compare Texas grama's short fuzzy bristly starbursts and hairy grama's broad combs. Inspect the individual spikelet awns and rolled leaves only with higher magnification.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole low small bunch with intact flowering axes and measured scale.
Fine narrow appressed branches against finger/black background; count them on ONE culm.
Dissected mature spikelet under lens revealing the awns, glumes and sterile floret (no inferred count).
Paired actual Texas grama fuzzy short branches and red grama narrow units at same scale.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Red grama's narrow reddish APPRESSED units on very fine wiry culms contrast with Texas grama's short clustered woolly/awned branches, hairy grama's broader stinger-bearing combs, and pectinata's robust long combs. measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: RED / THREE-AWNED GRAMA: trace 2–7 narrow, ascending-to-appressed one-sided branches on ONE wiry 10–40 cm perennial culm; each branch is roughly 12–25 mm long and has 8–24(–32) tightly set spikelets. Then dissect one 4–5 mm mature spikelet to see the THREE awns of its lower fertile lemma. Red color alone is not an ID.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form: Low tufted perennial; short rhizomes may be present, never assume an annual from a small drought-stressed plant. Mostly basal fine blades roughly 1–1.5 mm wide; ligule a HAIR FRINGE at the true inner blade–sheath junction, not a long projecting membrane. Source treatment does not provide a defensible ligule-mm measurement; obtain a calibrated macro before adding one.

reproductive_measurements.flowering_architecture: 2–7 unilateral branches, each 12–25 mm long; 8–24(–32) sessile spikelets per branch; branches ascend or hug the main axis.
reproductive_measurements.spikelets: Approximately 4–5 mm long, laterally compressed; one fertile basal floret plus a diminished upper floret. Spikelet length EXCLUDES the long awns.
reproductive_measurements.glumes: Lower glume 3–4 mm, upper glume 4–5 mm; both persistent, membranous and one-veined; upper longer than lower.
reproductive_measurements.fertile_lemma: Approximately 2 mm body, three-veined, often hairy at base (hairs ~0.2–0.5 mm); deeply three-lobed tip ending in THREE awns, central and lateral about 3–4 mm in GrassBase.
reproductive_measurements.upper_reduced_floret: Diminished apical floret also can carry awns. Do not mistake its awns for additional awns on the basal fertile lemma; separate florets before arrow placement.
reproductive_measurements.awns: Three awns belong to the fertile lemma, not the glumes or a separate Aristida-like single floret. Kew GrassBase gives ~3–4 mm; other regional treatments describe broader 2–8 mm variation.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Bouteloua pectinata is more robust with longer combs, but branch number and bare rachis tip can overlap; B. hirsuta has broad combs, often papillose-based hairs and a terminal bare rachis extension; B. dactyloides and B. gracilis have different growth/comb patterns. Inspect attached florets, not reddish hue.
last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: Same legally collected local specimen: rooted perennial tuft, short rhizome if present, whole 10–40 cm flowering culm and branch count with centimeter scale.
Entire attached 12–25 mm one-sided branch with spikelet count and tip against millimeter ruler; source photographs show gross branches but not reliably measured microstructures.
At 10–20×, one intact 4–5 mm spikelet with 1-mm scale, then separately expose the 3–4 mm lower and 4–5 mm upper glumes and the ~2 mm fertile lemma.
Detached fertile lemma showing three distinct awn origins (each ~3–4 mm in Kew), plus separate upper reduced floret; verify each arrow endpoint against actual pixels.
True hair-fringe ligule/collar with calibrated 0.5-mm scale; matched same-scale B. hirsuta and B. pectinata spikelets.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Keep FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS. FINISHED requires exact-species, rights-cleared real photographs of the branch and measured reproductive/collar organs, pixel-verified arrow endpoints and successful public learner QA. Preserve all seven original images, individual rights, prior annotations, original taxonomy and county-native decisions.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.evidence_scope: Species-specific GrassBase/Kew and Texas A&M published morphology, NOT direct measurements from the seven existing photos. No new images or arrows were added.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — SHORT, APPRESSED RED-GRAMA BRANCHES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Follow ONE wiry perennial flowering culm: usually 2–7 slender one-sided branches hugging the axis.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published ranges place flowering culms around 10–40 cm and individual branches around 12–25 mm. Existing species panels 1–3 show thin, often reddish ascending-to-appressed branches; color is variable and cannot establish the species. Count branches on a single attached flowering stem rather than across overlapping stems.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL BRANCH ARCHITECTURE — CONNECTED RULER-SCALED CULM NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · LOW PERENNIAL TUFT AND TRUE HAIR LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Small tufted perennial with narrow basal blades; true ligule is a short HAIR FRINGE.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The measured source describes blades commonly about 1–1.5 mm wide and occasional short rhizomes. Examine a blade–sheath junction from the SAME flowering plant to see the true ligule hairs rather than hairs on the sheath edge. No defensible species-specific ligule length in millimeters is established in the current evidence; do not invent one or arrow an unresolved fringe.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE-BASED GROWTH FORM — CALIBRATED TRUE LIGULE MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE ONE COMPLETE FLOWERING BRANCH
field_id_short_tiles.short: Each 12–25 mm one-sided branch often carries 8–24(–32) crowded spikelets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Use an intact attached branch and millimeter scale. Mature spikelets are about 4–5 mm long, excluding projecting awns; count spikelets on one branch. Existing close photographs show branch shape but do not establish exact counts or glume lengths. Never measure a long awn as part of the spikelet body.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL BRANCH PHOTOS — MATURE CALIBRATED SPIKELET GAP

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · TWO GLUMES AND THREE FERTILE-LEMMA AWNS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Spikelet ~4–5 mm; lower glume ~3–4 mm, upper ~4–5 mm; fertile lemma body ~2 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The paired one-veined glumes persist below a basal fertile floret and a diminished upper floret. A mature fertile lemma is three-veined and deeply three-lobed, bearing THREE awns typically ~3–4 mm in Kew's treatment; the reduced upper floret may ALSO bear awns. Separate both florets under 10–20× before assigning any awn to the fertile lemma. Awn count and exact origin are NOT pixel-verified in the existing wide photographs.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED DISSECTION CHARACTERS — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO AND NO MICRO ARROWS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Texas grama has short fuzzy clusters; hairy grama has broader combs and a bare tip stinger.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Comparison panel 6 is Bouteloua rigidiseta (Texas grama), NOT red grama. Hairy grama B. hirsuta and B. pectinata usually show broader combs; blue grama B. gracilis has curved eyebrow-like combs. The thin, reddish branches are only a first clue: confirm glumes and the three fertile-lemma awns to separate overlapping mature material. Avoid forcing species ID from red color.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL LOOK-ALIKE COMPARISON — MATCHED MATURE ANATOMY MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / TWO HANDOFFS
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: seven retained photo records, but ligule and three-awn origins remain unproven.
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO (Grass Photo-Finish): voucher-linked rooted Central Texas perennial and full 10–40 cm flowering culm; 12–25 mm attached branch and mature ~4–5 mm spikelets with 1-mm scale; both glumes, fertile three-awned lemma and separate reduced upper floret dissected at 10–20×; true hair-fringe ligule with 0.5-mm reference; same-scale Texas/hairy grama comparisons. NEEDS_SITE_QA (Public Learner Readiness): verify five locally archived images plus two external reference records, source IDs and per-image CC BY/CC BY-NC/public-domain terms, existing arrows, other-species panel labels, six-tile mobile layout and public page. Do not mark FINISHED or claim newly verified photos or arrows.

grass_species_finalization_20261025.look_here_first: Red grama: 2–7 narrow appressed branches on one wiry perennial culm, then confirm the THREE awns actually attached to the basal fertile lemma; reddish color alone is not diagnostic.
grass_species_finalization_20261025.measured_growth_and_collar: Tufted perennial, flowering culms ~10–40 cm; narrow basal blades ~1–1.5 mm, occasionally short rhizomes. True ligule is a hair fringe; no verified species-specific mm length, and existing images do not expose the true junction.
grass_species_finalization_20261025.measured_spikelet_glume_lemma_awn: Branches ~12–25 mm, often 8–24(–32) spikelets; spikelets ~4–5 mm without awns; lower glume ~3–4 mm, upper ~4–5 mm; fertile lemma body ~2 mm and three awns ~3–4 mm (published Kew treatment); reduced upper floret may also be awned. No photo-derived microscopic measurement.
grass_species_finalization_20261025.local_lookalikes: B. rigidiseta shorter fuzzy units; B. hirsuta broader combs with bare terminal rachis; B. pectinata robust long combs; B. gracilis curved eyebrows. Confirm actual attached lemma/awn origin.
